bug_semantics: An unauthenticated request to /api/<unrecognized-provider>/<path> reaches the dynamic provider route's default branch, which calls proxyHandler. proxyHandler constructs its fetch destination directly from the attacker-controlled x-base-url header plus attacker-controlled path/query data, performs the server-side fetch without an allowlist or private/loopback-address rejection, and streams the upstream response back. An attacker can therefore make the NextChat server request arbitrary external or internal resources, including loopback and cloud metadata endpoints.
flaw_origin: Commit f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650 is the atomic first writer of the vulnerable mechanism: it adds app/api/proxy.ts with fetchUrl derived from req.headers.get("x-base-url") and fetch(fetchUrl, ...), and in the same commit changes app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts so unknown providers default to that proxyHandler. The pre-existing route instead sent its default branch to the fixed OpenAI handler, and app/api/proxy.ts did not exist in the immediate parent.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file commit f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650` shows human author and committer `lloydzhou <lloydzhou@qq.com>` and the message `plugin add auth config`, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: Disclosure and attack path: https://github.com/ChatGPTNextWeb/NextChat/issues/6742 (open, created 2026-04-07) gives the unauthenticated `/api/unknown-provider/get` PoC with `x-base-url`, identifies the fallback-to-proxy path, and lists patched versions as `<None>`; https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ff75-fg5h-fjx7 identifies CVE-2026-7177, proxyHandler, SSRF, versions through 2.16.1, and says the project had not responded. BIC: in the assigned clone, `git show --format=fuller --patch f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650 -- 'app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts' app/api/proxy.ts` shows the one-parent 2024-09-02 commit simultaneously adding the header-derived `fetchUrl`/server-side `fetch` implementation and replacing the unknown-provider OpenAI default with proxyHandler. `git log -L 16,22:app/api/proxy.ts` attributes the vulnerable URL construction to f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650; repository-wide `git log --all -S'x-base-url'` and route-specific `git log --all -S'return proxyHandler(req, { params });'` independently lead to that commit (the only later x-base-url hit, 2b0f2e5f9d064bc8107414b0c2e7efe61c03cdef, merely adds DALL-E authorization behavior and retains the arbitrary destination). Parent absence: `git show b2965e1deb48f9e63aabecb1d477185d22f19e1f:'app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts'` shows unknown providers going only to openaiHandler, while `git cat-file -e b2965e1deb48f9e63aabecb1d477185d22f19e1f:app/api/proxy.ts` fails because that path is absent. Release boundary: `git tag --contains f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650 --sort=version:refname` begins at v2.15.0 and continues through the latest tag v2.16.1; `git show v2.14.2:'app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts'` shows the safe OpenAI default, whereas the same command at v2.15.0 shows the vulnerable proxyHandler default. The tag commits are v2.14.2=495b321d0afa9e23a256fde18f1d2ec60c54e34b, v2.15.0=fe5a4f4447a14c8864bbad26ec10651a338886c2, and v2.16.1=557a2cce357749c6fb3176d42e03ff6f7de4d355. Unpatched boundary: `git show defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0:'app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts'` and `git show defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0:app/api/proxy.ts` show that the 2026-08-11 main tip still has the unknown-provider proxy fallback and unvalidated x-base-url fetch; `git log --all --since='2026-04-07T00:00:00Z' -- app/api/proxy.ts 'app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts'` is empty. AI check: `git cat-file commit f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650` yields tree 206cf249917ff619323a2d9ca58e96cd34030404, the stated parent, human author/committer lloydzhou, and only the plain subject, with no AI attribution.
reasoning: The security boundary is not merely the existence of a configurable proxy: exploitation requires both the public unknown-provider fallback and the proxy's trust in x-base-url. The smallest commit that first makes that complete attack path real is f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650 because it writes both halves together; its direct parent lacks both the proxy file and the fallback. This is an ordinary single-parent source commit rather than a move, revert, release/backport, or later aggregate, so no decomposition is warranted. Git line history and two independent -S searches corroborate it. v2.14.2 is directly verified unaffected and v2.15.0 is the first tagged affected release; every later tag through the advisory's v2.16.1 ceiling contains the BIC. The disclosure remains open and the latest main tree remains vulnerable, so no fix SHA can truthfully be supplied. Finally, the BIC commit object has no qualifying AI attribution and uses a human author/committer identity; under the required BIC-only rule, later history or disclosure text cannot change the NOT_AI verdict.
remaining_gap: Unpatched as of 2026-08-28: no upstream fix or patched release exists to identify, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are necessarily null. The open disclosure, explicit `<None>` patched-version statement, unchanged 2026-08-11 main tip, and absence of post-disclosure changes to either vulnerable file establish this as an unpatched boundary rather than an evidence gap in locating a fix.
